//: THE BUDSCAN DISTRIBUTION POLICY. budscan.cfg sets the locked preferences; this file is the enterprise policy layer and is applied before the preferences. The two have to say the same thing: a setting that differs between the two layers makes it unreadable which one wins.

policies.//_telemetry: A browser reporting what it sees is doing the very thing it avoids. It is off in the policy layer too, in the same direction as the lockPref in budscan.cfg.
policies.//_crash: A crash report is a memory dump; it can carry the bytes of verified content out.
policies.//_update: Updates stay on. A browser that is not updated cannot sustain its verification claim.
policies.//_signature: An unsigned extension cannot be loaded. Unverified code running in a privileged context would make everything the badge measures meaningless.
policies.//_firstrun: No request goes out on the first run.
policies.//_search: Arama onerileri her tus vurusunu bir sunucuya gonderir.
policies.//_dns: DNS-over-HTTPS is left off: resolving bud:// names belongs to the budscan core, and handing that to a DoH provider would move the proof of resolution to a third party.
policies.//_passwords: The built-in password manager is off; a verification browser doubling as a credential store is a separate attack surface.
policies.//_tracking: Strict tracker protection as policy, not as a default the user can change.
policies.//_cleanup: Session data is not cleared on shutdown: that is the user's own preference and it does not break the verification claim. Leaving it free is deliberate.
